applicationInfo.name: Threat Model Export
applicationInfo.description: Sample application demonstrating AWS DevOps Agent investigating live AWS infrastructure incidents. Deploys a serverless order processing service (API Gateway + Lambda + DynamoDB) with fault injection scripts for 4 demo scenarios (throttling, cascading failure, code bug, infrastructure misconfiguration). CloudWatch alarms trigger SNS notifications forwarded via webhook to DevOps Agent Event Channels for autonomous investigation. The code is intended for public publication on aws-samples GitHub as educational/demonstration material.

assumptions.content: This is sample/demo code not intended for production use
No real customer PII or payment data is processed
The webhook secret and API endpoint are user-configured placeholders
Fault injection scripts are intentionally insecure by design

mitigations.content: API Gateway throttling and rate limiting configured via usage plans
Webhook secret stored as Lambda environment variable (user-configured)
CORS configuration (wildcard for demo purposes; should be restricted in production)
Input validation via Pydantic models for order creation requests
IAM least-privilege roles for Lambda execution (scoped to specific DynamoDB tables)
DynamoDB encryption at rest enabled by default
CORS configuration should be restricted to specific origins in production use

threats.prerequisites: with network access to the public API endpoint
threats.threatAction: flood the API with requests causing throttling
threats.threatImpact: service unavailability for legitimate demo users
threats.statement: A External attacker with network access to the public API endpoint can flood the API with requests causing throttling, which leads to service unavailability for legitimate demo users

threats.prerequisites: with access to Lambda environment variables
threats.threatAction: extract webhook secret from Lambda configuration
threats.threatImpact: ability to send fake alerts to DevOps Agent
threats.statement: A Malicious insider with access to Lambda environment variables can extract webhook secret from Lambda configuration, which leads to ability to send fake alerts to DevOps Agent

threats.threatAction: send crafted orders with invalid data to API
threats.threatImpact: corrupt demo data in DynamoDB tables
threats.statement: A External attacker with network access can send crafted orders with invalid data to API, which leads to corrupt demo data in DynamoDB tables

threats.threatAction: modify Lambda code to inject malicious logic
threats.threatImpact: compromised application behavior and data integrity
threats.statement: A Malicious insider with Lambda deployment permissions can modify Lambda code to inject malicious logic, which leads to compromised application behavior and data integrity

threats.prerequisites: with AWS console or API access
threats.threatAction: read demo order data from DynamoDB tables
threats.threatImpact: exposure of synthetic test data (no real PII)
threats.statement: A Unauthorized user with AWS console or API access can read demo order data from DynamoDB tables, which leads to exposure of synthetic test data (no real PII)

threats.threatAction: exploit wildcard CORS to perform cross-origin attacks
threats.threatImpact: unauthorized API access from malicious web pages
threats.statement: A External attacker with network access to API can exploit wildcard CORS to perform cross-origin attacks, which leads to unauthorized API access from malicious web pages
